This neuron is essentially a "verb-phrase-ellipsis detector" in reverse: it is driven most strongly *negative* at the end of anaphoric/elliptical clauses where "do/did/that" stands in for a full predicate ("I did.", "so I do,", "and I **do** need", "none of that **happened**"), while its (weak) positive activations fall on the ordinary word that overtly completes such a phrase instead ("did a **search**", "the four **that**", "which was **enacted**").

L7·N8496unmasked layer
This neuron (whose positive range is tiny; its strong signal is negative) peaks on the word completing a short prepositional/possessive noun phrase in informal marketing-style prose — typically a personal pronoun or the second piece of a proper name/brand right after "of"/"for" (of **my** heart, for AG**RA**, ui u**Learn**, of **yourself**, for **film**) — while being strongly suppressed on the tail sub-word of technical compound nouns (Vent**ilation**, dry**wall**, buy-s**ell**, "partly **chilled**").
